Beech rotation (110–140 yr, or 80–100 yr in some countries): Analysis and evaluation of the impact of stand age on the occurrence and metamorphosis of red heartwood — iForest, 2017 (https://iforest.sisef.org/contents/?id=ifor2116-010)
comments: There is a large range for hardwood rotation periods. Normally they are 100+ years, but optimized forests can be as quick as 20 years. See Short-rotation hardwood paper (8–20 yr): Fuels of the Future for Renewable Energy Sources review (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.00439)

rotationPeriod_source: Softwood CORRIM figure: Cradle-to-gate LCA of softwood lumber production, NE-NC region (https://corrim.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/NENC-Lumber-LCA-final-May-2013.pdf)

carbonContent_source: The seagrass carbon content of 0.336 of dry weight can be applied in Indonesian seagrasses — Rahmawati, Hernawan & Rustam, AIP Conference Proceedings, 2019 (https://pubs.aip.org/aip/acp/article/2120/1/030012/1024597/The-seagrass-carbon-content-of-0-336-of-dry-weight)

material_name: If the material is a (co-) product, then the benefit is carbon sequestration (GWPbio method that includes both storage and rotation period)
If material is a waste / wild-harvested product, then the benefit is delayed carbon emissions (GWPbio method that only includes storage period)
on carbon content: beware that it is dry weight, so you need to take into account the water content. this info is available in ecoinvent.

carbonContent_source: derived: 0.45 kgC per kg pea (IPCC Tier 1 / Lal 2004) x 0.5893 kg peas per kg binder (biopol_lca LCI: peas -> isolate -> binder)
